title: Lab-in-the-Loop at Compute Speed — Ian Quigley, Leash Bio
author: Brandon Anderson
description: How Leash Bio tamed DELs, the assay that traumatizes everyone, and used the data to catch cheating models. And why that same data is perfect for AI agents learning to think like chemists.
summary: A few years ago I stumbled upon Leash Bio’s Substack , and was hooked. Be it their Kaggle competition that showed that no, we really haven’t solved protein-ligand binding , or their crazy discovery that knowing a molecule’s author is perhaps all you need to know to predict how good it is .
takeaways: Near the end of this episode, Ian teases something his team was just playing with when we recorded: an AI playground for agents to do verifiable scientific reasoning.
The agent sandbox : LLMs that reason about SAR in plain English, hunting for the best binders among 6.5M molecules on a budget of 100.
Their substack — or at least Owl Posting ’s 1 deep dive on them — should be required reading for any scientist trying to do chemistry with AI.
